VAN.head: We gave Vancouver only a 37% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Vancouver got the good looks
surprises.body: San Jose usually allows more dangerous shots than most teams. Even by those standards, this was a night of good looks: Vancouver’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 9.9% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.4% (about 6.6% against San Jose) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 50 games.

story.head: Smith’s two goals spark the Sharks
paras: Filip Bystedt played his first NHL game. Drew O'Connor got the scoring started for the Canucks midway through the first. Liam Öhgren made it 2-0 late in the second, and that was all they would get. Will Smith scored twice and Mason Marchment once in just under three minutes midway through the third to put the Sharks ahead for good and complete the comeback.

Nothing much separated these two on the chances. This one could have gone either way. Yaroslav Askarov made 23 saves for the Sharks, and Leevi Meriläinen stopped 21 of 24 at the other end. The Sharks improved to 7-6-1, fourth in the Pacific, while the Canucks dropped to 3-11-1, still last in the NHL.
